high.title: T-bill yields mixed as central bank stays hawkish
high.summary: The Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) successfully raised the full P50 billion target from its T-bill auction on Monday, drawing strong demand with total tenders reaching P126.091 billion — more than twice the offered amount, though slightly below the previous auction's P136.841 billion in bids. Yields came in mixed, reflecting the market's attempt to reprice short-duration government paper against a backdrop of continued hawkish signals from the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP). The hawkish BSP stance suggests the central bank is in no rush to ease policy rates, which has direct implications for the short end of the yield curve. Bond investors should note that while demand remains robust — indicating strong domestic liquidity — the mixed yield outcome signals some uncertainty about the near-term rate trajectory. The concurrent geopolitical risk from renewed US-Iran hostilities is also adding a risk-averse tone to market positioning. **Key watch:** Any further BSP communication on the timing of rate cuts will be critical in determining whether short-end yields compress or continue to drift higher in coming auctions.

high.title: Peso weakens on Middle East clashes
high.summary: The Philippine Peso depreciated by 8.4 centavos against the US Dollar on Monday, closing at **P61.599/USD** from Friday's close of P61.515, as renewed US-Iran military exchanges triggered a broad flight-to-safety bid for the greenback. The Peso opened the session weaker at P61.61 and managed an intraday high of P61.56, suggesting limited relief rallies amid persistent geopolitical risk aversion. This move is consistent with broader emerging market FX weakness during episodes of Middle East-driven risk-off sentiment, where USD demand typically accelerates. For PHP traders, the key risk is whether escalating US-Iran tensions sustain elevated oil prices — a negative double shock for the Philippines as a net oil importer, which would widen the trade deficit and add imported inflationary pressure, compounding pressure on the Peso. **Key watch:** Monitor oil price trajectory and any BSP intervention signals at the P61.60–P62.00 range; a breach of P62.00 could invite more active BSP defense of the currency.

high.title: Two More 25-bp Rate Hikes Seen This Year
high.summary:
Deutsche Bank Research is projecting two additional 25-basis-point rate hikes by the Bangko Sentral ng Pilipinas (BSP) at its August 27 and October 22 policy meetings. The call is driven by broadening price pressures even as headline inflation eased to a three-month low of 6.4% in June. Critically, core inflation — which strips out volatile food and energy components — remains elevated, signaling that underlying demand-side price pressures have not yet meaningfully subsided, justifying a continued tightening bias.

**Market Implications:** For PHP traders, additional rate hikes are broadly supportive of the peso as a higher policy rate differential vs. the USD could attract short-term portfolio inflows. However, if hikes are perceived as insufficient to anchor inflation expectations, PHP could remain under pressure. For bond investors, two more hikes imply further upward pressure on the short-to-mid end of the yield curve — watch for steepening dynamics. PSEi may face headwinds as higher borrowing costs compress equity valuations, particularly for rate-sensitive sectors. The August 27 meeting is the immediate key catalyst to monitor.

high.title: T-bill and Bond Rates May Be Mixed as Conflict Weighs
high.summary:
Yields at this week's Bureau of the Treasury (BTr) auctions — P50 billion in T-bills (Monday) and P30 billion in reissued 10-year T-bonds (Tuesday) — are expected to be mixed, with dual headwinds from renewed Middle East conflict uncertainty and hawkish BSP signals. The T-bill offering is split across 91-day (P20B), 182-day (P20B), and 364-day (P10B) tenors, while the T-bond auction tests appetite at the long end of the curve.

**Market Implications:** The hawkish BSP backdrop (see Deutsche Bank call above) may push short-end T-bill yields higher, while geopolitical risk — typically a flight-to-safety driver — could provide some offsetting demand for longer-dated securities. Bond investors should watch auction bid-to-cover ratios closely as a gauge of real-money demand and market confidence in the rate outlook. Weak auction results would signal further yield upside and potential mark-to-market losses for existing bond holders. PHP may also face volatility if geopolitical risk appetite deteriorates sharply heading into the week.

high.title: Season of Selling to End Philippine Peso Rally, Strategists Say
high.summary:
The Philippine peso's recent relief rally — triggered by the initial US-Iran ceasefire — is expected to be short-lived, according to strategists, as structural seasonal forces reassert themselves. Bloomberg data spanning the past decade show the peso has depreciated an average of 1.6% against the US dollar during Q3, making it the worst-performing quarter for the currency on a seasonal basis. The primary driver is corporate dollar demand: local firms ramp up import payments ahead of the year-end peak business season, creating sustained pressure on the peso. For FX traders, this is a critical signal — any near-term strength in PHP should be viewed as a selling opportunity rather than a trend reversal. The ceasefire-driven relief rally may have temporarily masked underlying vulnerabilities. PHP traders should monitor the pace of corporate dollar buying, BSP intervention activity, and any deterioration in the current account as import demand picks up. A retest of record lows in PHP/USD remains a credible base case through Q3 2026. Bond investors should also factor in potential inflationary pass-through from a weaker peso.

---

medium.title: Banks could face sanctions under financial consumer protection law
medium.summary: The BSP has released a draft circular to implement Republic Act No. 11765 (the Financial Products and Services Consumer Protection Act, or FCPA), outlining administrative sanctions, penalties, stop orders, and potential suspension for non-compliant banks and financial institutions. While this is primarily a regulatory/compliance development rather than a direct macro or FX catalyst, it carries medium-term significance for the banking sector's operational risk profile and cost of compliance. Stricter enforcement could impact profitability margins for smaller banks, with potential read-through to lending activity and credit availability. Fund managers with exposure to Philippine bank equities listed on the PSEi should monitor the final circular's scope and penalty thresholds closely.

medium.title: BDO closes bond offering early amid robust demand
medium.summary: BDO Unibank closed its 1.5-year ASEAN Sustainability Bond public offering on Friday — a full week ahead of the original July 21 schedule — citing strong demand from both retail and institutional investors, with settlement and listing still set for July 28. The early closure is a positive signal for domestic fixed-income market depth and investor appetite for peso-denominated bank paper. Strong demand for BDO's issuance, even amid a hawkish BSP backdrop and geopolitical uncertainty, suggests domestic liquidity remains ample and that sustainability-themed instruments are gaining traction in the Philippine market. This has indirect relevance for government bond demand dynamics and overall peso fixed-income sentiment.

medium.title: BSP's Open Market Operations Mop Up P1.3 Trillion in Cash from Financial System
medium.summary:
The BSP has absorbed P1.3 trillion in excess liquidity from the financial system through open market operations as of June 9, according to its June 2026 Monetary Policy Report. The operations have been effective in keeping the overnight reverse repurchase (RRP) rate aligned with the BSP's policy target, reinforcing the transmission of monetary tightening into broader financial conditions. For FX and rates traders, this is an important confirmation that BSP's tightening cycle is operationally effective — excess liquidity is being drained, which should support the peso by reducing inflationary monetary overhang. Combined with the anticipated additional rate hikes, this signals a consistent and credible tightening posture from the central bank, which is a mild positive for PHP and a headwind for bond prices at the short end of the curve.

---

medium.title: PSEi Edges Lower as US, Iran Exchange Attacks
medium.summary: The PSEi fell 0.33% (20.98 points) to close at 6,265.72 on Monday, with the broader all-shares index also declining 0.29% to 3,383.23, as investors adopted a risk-off stance amid ongoing US-Iran geopolitical tensions and the absence of fresh positive catalysts. The market traded in a consolidation pattern, suggesting investors are reluctant to build new positions until the geopolitical picture clarifies. For equity investors, the PSEi remains range-bound near the 6,200–6,300 zone; continued Middle East escalation could weigh further on sentiment and trigger foreign outflows, adding indirect pressure on the PHP. Watch for any shift in foreign net buying/selling data as a leading indicator of capital flow direction.

medium.title: Continued Bargain Hunting to Support PHL Stocks
medium.summary: The PSEi posted its best close in over four months on Friday, July 11, jumping 1.01% (62.83 points) to 6,286.70, buoyed by bargain hunting activity. On a week-on-week basis, the index recorded meaningful gains, suggesting some recovery momentum. However, analysts cautioned that renewed Middle East tensions and a lack of fresh domestic catalysts could limit upside and keep investors in a wait-and-see mode for the week ahead. For fund managers, the technical recovery is encouraging but fragile — sustained foreign inflows would be needed to confirm a more durable trend, and geopolitical risk remains the key swing factor for both equities and the peso.

medium.title: Stocks Snap Six-Day Run on Middle East, Growth Concerns
medium.summary: The PSEi broke a six-consecutive-session winning streak on Thursday, July 9, falling 0.82% (51.90 points) to 6,223.87, as profit-taking combined with reignited US-Iran tensions and softening economic growth prospects dampened sentiment. The broader all-shares index fell a sharper 1.01% to 3,370.56, indicating broad-based selling. The pullback underscores the market's sensitivity to external geopolitical shocks and macro headwinds. For investors, this reinforces the view that the PSEi rally lacked strong fundamental conviction and that downside risks remain elevated should geopolitical conditions deteriorate further or domestic growth data disappoint.

medium.title: Stocks up for fifth straight day on slower inflation
medium.summary: Philippine equities extended their winning streak to five consecutive sessions, with the PSEi climbing 0.37% (+23.12 points) to close at 6,247.11 — a three-week high. The key driver was the release of June 2026 inflation data, which came in softer than expected, lifting investor sentiment broadly. For macro traders, easing inflation is a critical signal: it reinforces the case for continued BSP rate cuts, which would be supportive of both equities and bonds. Softer CPI also reduces upward pressure on the PHP, though a rate-cut trajectory could limit peso appreciation. Bond investors should watch whether the BSP signals a policy response to this inflation print at its next Monetary Board meeting. The inflation-driven equity rally suggests the market is pricing in a more dovish BSP stance ahead.

medium.title: Shares hit four-month high on sustained buying
medium.summary: The PSEi rose 0.45% (+28.66 points) to 6,275.77 on Wednesday — its highest close since March 6, 2026 — marking a sixth consecutive session of gains. The rally persisted despite renewed US-Iran geopolitical tensions, which typically prompt risk-off sentiment in emerging markets. The resilience of Philippine equities in the face of external headwinds suggests domestic macro tailwinds (i.e., easing inflation expectations and potential BSP accommodation) are currently dominating sentiment. For fund managers, the six-day winning streak and the breach of a four-month high may attract incremental foreign portfolio inflows, which would be mildly supportive of the PHP. Watch foreign net buying/selling data from the PSE for confirmation of offshore participation.

medium.title: PSEi hits near 3-week high before inflation data
medium.summary: The PSEi climbed 0.58% (+35.96 points) to 6,223.99, returning to the 6,200 level for the first time in nearly three weeks, driven by pre-inflation data optimism. Markets were anticipating a further easing in June CPI, which subsequently materialized in the following session's report. The pre-positioning dynamic is relevant for fixed income and FX traders: expectations of lower inflation were already being priced into equities, suggesting bond markets may have similarly seen yield compression ahead of the print. This article provides useful context for understanding the inflation-driven market narrative that dominated the week.
